title: Test-Time Guidance for Flow-Based Generative Models via Parallel Tempering on Source Distributions
claim: A baseline guidance method misses the high-reward mode of a multimodal target, while ours recovers it, with a consistent advantage across settings.
layout: 3 panels left-to-right: two density plots, then a line plot; W2 in captions
description: Three side-by-side plots. Panels (a) and (b) are 1-D density plots on a log y-axis. Each shows a bimodal base distribution p(x) as a green dashed curve, with a large mode near x=-1.5 and a small one near x=1.5. A tall, narrow black spike at x≈1.5 marks the tilted target p~(x). In (a), FK Steering samples are a blue histogram sitting on the wrong, low-reward left mode, with W2 = 2.98. In (b), SPT samples are an orange spike that lands on the target spike, with W2 = 0.09. Panel (c) plots W2 distance against ω² on a log x-axis. The FK Steering line, in blue with stars, falls from about 1.1 to 0.2. The SPT line, in orange with dots, stays near zero. Blue and orange separate the methods. The eye goes first to the tall black spike and the sample mismatch in (a).
caption: Panel (a) shows a sample where FK Steering fails to capture the high-reward mode of the tilted distribution ˜p(x) in equation 14
abstract: Generative models that transport a simple source distribution to a complex data distribution—such as diffusion and flow-based models—are central to high‑fidelity data generation. Test-time guidance can further steer pretrained models toward user-specified high-reward regions without costly retraining. However, existing guidance methods face critical limitations: they struggle with non-differentiable rewards, fail to navigate complex landscapes, and often lack theoretical guarantees on generation performance. We propose {\it Source Parallel Tempering (SPT)}, a gradient‑free test‑time guidance framework that operates entirely in source space, leveraging its simpler geometry to avoid the complexities of the data manifold. SPT couples a local exploration kernel with parallel tempering, enabling efficient barrier crossing and robust discovery of high‑reward modes. Theoretically, we provide a new error bound linking training-time approximation error to test-time guidance performance.Empirically, SPT significantly improves over state-of-the-art methods on benchmark tasks in conditional image synthesis and dynamical system trajectory sampling.
